title: 5.5.1 Plan: Break Snake into parts
description: Before any code: list the parts of Snake, what the game must remember between frames, what to build first and what looks hard. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is on this page and in 5.4.7 (Lab: Crash, and start again): go back and reread it if you get stuck. A few short sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

You are about to build Snake. Before you write any code, plan it.

1. List at least four separate parts of the game, things it has or does.

2. Which two or more things does the game have to remember from one frame to the next?

3. Which part would you build first, and why?

4. Which part are you unsure how to build, and what makes it hard?

rubric.title: Four or more parts of the game are named
rubric.description: The student names at least four separate parts of Snake in their own words, such as the snake's cells, the food, steering, the beat that moves it, scoring, losing, and restarting. Credit any plausible list of four or more, however loosely worded. A part is something the game has or does; a list that only restates the rules in one lump is partial.

rubric.title: Says what the game must remember between frames
rubric.description: The student names at least two things the game has to remember from one frame to the next, for example where every cell of the snake is, which way it is heading, where the food is, the score, and whether the round is still playing. Any two sensible items earn full credit.

rubric.title: Picks a first thing to build and gives a reason
rubric.description: The student says which part they would build first and gives any reason at all (it is the base the rest sits on, it is the easiest to test, nothing else works without it). Be generous: a short plausible reason is enough.

rubric.title: Names one part they are unsure how to build
rubric.description: The student names one part they do not yet know how to do, such as growing the body or making the snake not bite itself, and says in a few words what is hard about it. Any honest, specific answer counts; 'nothing' or a blank is the only miss.
